segments.text: "Alert me if someone steals." Obvious to a person. But there's no obvious way to train a model for it.
No dataset defines theft. So cameras just record, and the tape gets reviewed after the loss.
Meet Lookout. A visual harness for NVIDIA Nemotron.
Describe the behaviour in plain Markdown, step by step. That's a skill.
Nemotron reads the frames, judges every step and its order, and takes a closer look when a moment is unclear.
When it happens, you get an alert, with timestamped proof.
Change a sentence, and the monitor changes with it.
No dataset. No training. No ML team.
Loss prevention. Packing accuracy. Safety procedures. The people who know the rule write the monitor.
If you can describe it, Lookout can watch for it.
